messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: PROD elevated 5xx rate + streaming disconnects detected in us-west-2. Error rate: 4.5% (5m), streaming disconnect rate: 12% (5m). Primary symptoms: 502/504 gateway, chunked-stream connection resets, client cancellations. Runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-disconnects>

megan: getting inbound support tickets saying 'partial response then closed' from several customers using streaming SDK. Customers report reconnect loops.

omar (eng-sre): looking at gateway logs now, seeing lots of `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `502` from gateway->runtime. Example tail from gateway:```
[2026-03-15T14:02:23Z] proxy: upstream 10.0.3.45 timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client: 52.12.34.56, server: api.redwood, request: "GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-large HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.3.45:8080/stream", host: "api.redwood"
[2026-03-15T14:02:24Z] proxy: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 52.12.34.56, server: api.redwood, request: "GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-large HTTP/1.1"
```

ryan (runtime): runtime logs show frequent `write: broken pipe` and `client aborted` on streaming worker processes. Also seeing increased GC pause times on a subset of workers. Pasting worker snippet:```
[14:02:21] worker-7 ERROR: write: broken pipe (Errno::32) while sending chunk to client
[14:02:22] worker-7 INFO: connection closed by client, token_id=abc123, total_sent=3.4k tokens
[14:02:22] worker-7 WARN: kv-cache miss count spike -> increased disk io
```

sanjay (infra): LB health checks are green, but we see one gateway node with high socket errors and backlog. I've restarted gateway-ops-2 (10.0.1.12) once, still seeing errors. Scaling gateway pool by +2 now.

elena (oncall): I'm oncall, taking lead. Quick questions: is this isolated to streaming endpoints or is non-streaming generation also affected?

omar: non-streaming text generation error rate increased slightly (~0.8%) but not as bad. Streaming clearly hit hardest. Pattern: long-running streams (>20s) more likely to fail.

megan: support says top-aggravated customers are using chunked SSE clients. They see partial json then connection reset.

ryan: hypothesis: chunked transfer encoding interplay with gateway keepalive / upstream timeout causing premature resets. Also some runtime workers hitting memory pressure -> closing connections mid-stream.

omar: quickly tried increasing `proxy_read_timeout` on gateway from 30s -> 90s for upstream to avoid premature timeouts. Patch applied to gateway pool via config:```
upstream api_backend {
  server 10.0.3.40:8080;
  server 10.0.3.41:8080;
}
proxy_read_timeout 90s;
```

sanjay: rolled that to 3/4 gateway nodes (staged) — observing a small dip in 504 but streaming disconnects still around 9%.

elena: what's the immediate mitigation priority? reduce customer impact. Options: 1) route streaming traffic to older stable runtime variant (no chunked SSE) 2) throttle new streaming connections globally 3) disable chunked transfer at gateway and fall back to buffered responses 4) rollback recent runtime change (if any). Thoughts?

ryan: i vote option 3 short-term (disable chunked transfer) — will increase latency and memory usage but should avoid partial deliveries and client reconnect loops. Option 1 also possible but need quick routing tweak.

omar: there's a recent runtime deploy 20260315-proto-stream that touched streaming backpressure logic. We can rollback that if needed. Checking canary metrics now.

deploy-bot: Deploy roll history: 20260314-stable -> 20260315-proto-stream (20% traffic) -> 20260315-rollback available.

sanjay: we can route 100% streaming traffic to the stable ring in 2m. That will drop new sessions onto older codepath.

megan: do we have customer-facing messaging ready? I'll draft a brief note: 'We're aware of streaming interruptions; short-term workaround: switch to non-streaming requests or retry with backoff.'

elena: action plan for now: 1) backfill streaming traffic to stable ring (sanjay + deploy-bot) 2) disable chunked transfer at gateway for streaming endpoints (omar + ryan) 3) throttle new streaming connections by 30% (sanjay) 4) support to notify top impacted customers (megan).

omar: initiating gateway config change to set `chunked_transfer_encoding off;` for /v1/stream location on the staged gateways. Applying now.

ryan: also dropping `keepalive_timeout` from 75s -> 30s to reduce stale sockets on gateway temporarily.

deploy-bot: Routing change: shifting streaming traffic to stable ring; in progress (slot swap). Estimated 90s to complete.

[+90s]

omar: config pushed to staged gateways. Observed drop in partial-delivery errors on those nodes. Global stats: streaming disconnect rate reduced from 12% -> 5.8% after routing shift and chunked disable on 50% of gateways. Still above baseline.

sanjay: scaled streaming worker pool +20% and restarted 6/12 runtime pods that had high GC. Heap pressure improved on the restarted ones.

megan: support: customers #A, #B, #C report improvements after reconnecting. Others still report intermittent issues. Preparing status update to affected customers now.

elena: are we safe to keep these mitigations while we finish root cause? Any risk to stability?

ryan: risk: disabling chunked for streams increases memory and response buffering, might cause higher latency or OOM at very high concurrency — we need to monitor worker memory closely. Running autoscale and setting a hard cap on concurrent streams would help.

omar: i'm starting a canary rollback of 20260315-proto-stream (move streaming traffic off that variant) to see if error rate normalizes further.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for `20260315-proto-stream` ring -> switched streaming traffic 100% to stable.

[+120s]

omar: after rollback + chunked off + scaled workers, streaming disconnect rate now at 2.1% and overall 5xx down to 0.6%. Partial deliveries appear much lower.

megan: sending customer-facing note now. Draft: 'We experienced streaming interruptions in us-west-2 affecting partial responses. We've implemented mitigations (rollback + gateway config) and most customers report restored service. We're continuing investigation and will follow up with root cause and timeline.'

elena: good. Assigning postmortem owner: omar. Please capture timeline, configs changed, impact windows, customer list, and follow-up actions (increase runtime memory headroom, improve streaming health checks, regression test for chunked behavior).

omar: acknowledged. I'll open INC-196200 and link runbook + logs.

incident-bot: Incident INC-196200 opened. Severity: Sev2. Assigned: omar (eng-sre). Postmortem due in 72h.

elena: handing off to normal ops cadence — i'm still watching for 15m. If anything spikes, @oncall please page. Thanks all for fast responses :thumbsup:

megan: will follow up with support tickets and customer emails.

ryan: i'll add extra runtime metrics dashboard for chunked vs buffered streaming, memory per-worker, conn resets.

sanjay: keeping autoscale adjustments in flight for 30m.

omar: saving logs and snapshots to incident ticket. End-of-thread status: mitigations applied, error rates reduced to near-baseline, postmortem opened.

elena: closing live triage.
